ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 80% high-intensity (white/cream) to 20% low-intensity (black) pixel distribution across the visible ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant white contiguous fields on both lateral lobes; a prominent vertical low-intensity black band bisects the fluke at the median notch; dense black punctate mottling and stochastic speckling are concentrated along the trailing edge margins and distal tips.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with a calculated interior angle of approximately 42 degrees; notch depth extends approximately 12% into the total vertical height of the fluke structure.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Highly irregular, high-frequency serration pattern along the entire trailing boundary; pixel-amplitude of peaks and valleys ranges from 3 to 12 pixels, with maximum jaggedness observed on the distal tips of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Symmetrical convex curve originating from the median notch, flattening toward the mid-lobe, and terminating in an upward-sweeping convex curve at the outer tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense, high-contrast textured clusters (barnacles) localized on the extreme distal tips of both lobes; numerous small circular black-pixel spots (2-4 pixel diameter) distributed across the white ventral surface.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Multiple faint, unaligned dark linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) detected on the inner right lobe and sporadically on the central-left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive calcified biological encrustations on the distal tips of both lobes; highly irregular, asymmetrical trailing edge topography indicating significant mechanical wear or historical tissue loss.
other_distinctive_markers: Significant yellowish-brown low-intensity pixel staining (diatom biofilm) observed across the lower interior quadrants of both ventral lobes.
